passage:
Yogesh: Dhruv!! Rajma chawal tonight? I'm making too much anyway 😄
Dhruv: Yes!! And I need to tell you what happened in the lab today 😅
Yogesh: Tell tell tell. Wait, still coming to the movie tomorrow?
Dhruv: Actually I promised my old school friends I'd join their gaming night tomorrow. Sorry.
Yogesh: Oh. ...okay. I was kind of hoping we'd do everything together this month.
Yogesh: Ignore that, I'm being silly. Go, have fun.
Dhruv: Thanks. Saturday brunch, just us?
Yogesh: Yes please 🙂 Also I'll ask Kabir about the trek group, I've been sitting on that.

qa.q: What did Yogesh offer to make tonight?
What did Yogesh feel when Dhruv mentioned the gaming night, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Disappointed. Yogesh answers "Oh. ...okay" and admits hoping they would do everything together.

qa.q: What small step shows Yogesh keeping some independence from Dhruv?
qa.a: Telling Dhruv to go and have fun, keeping Saturday brunch, and planning to ask Kabir about a trek group so not all social needs rest on Dhruv.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel about Yogesh's reaction?
qa.a: Perhaps a little guilty at first, then relieved to hear "Go, have fun" and to have a brunch plan.

grounding: Yogesh and Dhruv become close and share meals and jokes, while Yogesh notices the pull to need Dhruv for everything and keeps independence.

passage:
You're asking about my roommate, Didi? Tenzin is the best thing about this college. First week, I was homesick, and he just put a bowl of thukpa in front of me and said, "Eat. Then complain."
Since then we've done everything together. Instant noodles at midnight, cricket at seven, the same electives. By second semester I noticed something: I'd stopped talking to anyone else. If Tenzin went to his Ladakhi students' meet, I'd sit in the room waiting, a bit sulky, like he owed me.
One Sunday he said, gently, "Vaibhav, come to the meet, or go to your quiz club. But don't sit waiting for me like this." It stung. He was right.
So I joined the quiz club. Now on Thursdays I have my people, he has his, and at eleven we compare notes over chai. It's better, honestly. I'm Vaibhav, still his biggest fan, just not his shadow.

qa.q: What did Tenzin put in front of Vaibhav in the first week?
How did Vaibhav feel when Tenzin went to the students' meet?
qa.a: Sulky and a bit lonely, waiting in the room as if Tenzin owed Vaibhav company.

qa.q: What changed after Tenzin's gentle comment?
qa.a: Vaibhav joined the quiz club and built a separate circle, while keeping the eleven o'clock chai with Tenzin.

qa.q: How did Tenzin see Vaibhav's waiting?
qa.a: As too much dependence; he cared about Vaibhav but wanted Vaibhav to have a life beyond their room.

grounding: Shows a close roommate friendship and learning to enjoy it while keeping independence, rather than expecting one person to fill every social need.

passage:
Week one: In the working women's hostel in Hyderabad, Sudha and Ishita discovered they both loved spicy pickle and old film songs. By Friday they were eating every dinner together on the floor of their room, laughing until the neighbours knocked.
Week four: On Saturday Ishita went to her office friends' dinner. Sudha, alone, texted her four times, "When are you back?", and sulked the next morning. Ishita said, "I love our dinners. But I can't be your only person." Sudha felt hurt, then embarrassed, because it was true: she hadn't called anyone else in weeks.
Week seven: Sudha had joined a Sunday pottery class and was slowly getting to know two women from it. On weekday nights she and Ishita still ate pickle and rice on the floor. On Saturdays they each went out, and came back with stories to swap.

qa.q: What did Sudha and Ishita both love?
qa.a: Spicy pickle and old film songs.

qa.q: How did Sudha feel after Ishita said "I can't be your only person"?
qa.a: Hurt at first, then embarrassed, realising she hadn't called anyone else in weeks.

qa.q: What did Sudha do to keep the friendship healthy?
qa.a: She joined a Sunday pottery class and got to know new people while keeping the weekday dinners with Ishita.

qa.q: How did Ishita feel about the four texts?
qa.a: Crowded and pressured; she loved their dinners but didn't want to be Sudha's only person.

grounding: Illustrates a warm roommate friendship over weeks and the shift from expecting one person to meet every need to keeping some independence.
